- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is neutral or negative, especially in the first 7–10 days of the forecast window.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price drops by forecasting a sharp rebound — adjust downward if sentiment is weak or flat.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after sustained upward momentum; reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment is cooling.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days prior, model should not overreact — dampen forecast if sentiment is fading.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high but price is falling, model should not assume continuation; reduce forecast slope.
- Horizon-specific: last 5–7 days of forecast are often overestimated — apply a 3–5% downward correction if sentiment is stable or declining.
